questions.q: How did David find his way to the first house on the Ross of Mull?
choices: He followed a road marked with stones
He aimed for the smoke he had seen from the island
He followed the fishers who had rescued him
He walked along the rocky shore until he saw a lamp burning
questions.evidence: I aimed as well as I could for the smoke I had seen so often from the island

questions.q: What news did the old gentleman at the house give David about his shipmates?
choices: That they had all been drowned in the wreck
That they had come ashore safe and eaten in that house
That red-coats had arrested them on the beach
That they had all sailed away to Ireland in the ship's skiff
questions.evidence: my shipmates had got safe ashore, and had broken bread in that very house

questions.q: Why did David smile when told the first man was bareheaded?
choices: He guessed Alan had hidden his fine hat from the rain
He thought Alan looked foolish without a hat
He knew it meant Alan had sold his hat for food
He was glad that Alan had finally stopped being so vain about clothes
questions.evidence: I judged it more likely he had it out of harm's way under his great-coat

questions.q: What message had been left for "the lad with the silver button"?
choices: To wait at the house until Alan came back
To follow his friend to his country, by Torosay
To take the next boat from Iona back home to Queensferry
To find Mr. Campbell the minister in Essendean
questions.evidence: you are to follow your friend to his country, by Torosay

questions.q: How did the old gentleman and his wife treat David?
choices: They fed him and then asked for most of his money
They fed him, let him sleep, and would take no money
They gave him a bed but sent him off before dawn
They were afraid of him and spoke to him through the door

questions.q: David thinks, "If these are the wild Highlanders, I could wish my own folk wilder." What does he mean?
choices: He wishes Lowlanders were as kind as these people
He thinks the Highlanders are much too rough
He wishes his own people were braver in battle
He fears the Highlanders will soon turn wild on him
questions.evidence: I could wish my own folk wilder

questions.q: Why were people on Mull dressed in such strange mixtures of clothes?
choices: The Highland dress had been forbidden by law
A fire had burned most of the island's cloth
It was the custom for a summer festival
Traders had stopped bringing cloth to the island
questions.evidence: The Highland dress being forbidden by law since the rebellion

questions.q: How did the Highland beggars differ from the Lowland beggars David knew?
choices: They stood on their dignity and would give no change
They begged only for bread and never for money
They sang songs and played pipes for every coin
They followed travellers for miles and would not leave
questions.evidence: these Highland beggars stood on their dignity

questions.q: What made the man at the lone house suddenly able to speak English?
choices: David spoke to him in French
David held up a guinea
His wife scolded him for being rude
David showed him Alan's silver button
questions.evidence: held up one of my guineas in my finger and thumb

questions.q: Why did David and his guide spend a whole night at Hector Maclean's house?
choices: A storm made the road to Torosay too dangerous
The guide got merry on punch and refused to start
Maclean needed a full day to gather and count out the silver
David was too ill with his sore throat to walk
questions.evidence: my rascal guide grew so merry that he refused to start

questions.q: After taking two more shillings and walking about two miles, what did the guide do?
choices: Ran off back toward Maclean's house
Sat down and took off his brogues to rest
Led David straight into a deep bog
Called some friends to rob David
questions.evidence: he sat down upon the wayside and took off his brogues from his feet

questions.q: How did the fight between David and the guide end?
choices: The guide cut David's arm with the knife and ran off into the hills
David knocked him down and took his knife and brogues
Hector Maclean arrived and stopped them fighting
David gave in and paid him three more shillings
questions.evidence: I picked up both that and his brogues

questions.q: The guide "took off his brogues from his feet," and David later leaves him "barefoot." What are brogues?
choices: Stockings
Shoes
Leg wraps
Spurs

questions.q: What did David notice that made him distrust the blind catechist?
choices: A pistol butt sticking out of his coat-pocket
A purse full of stolen guineas at his belt
A red-coat's badge pinned inside his cloak
A knife hidden inside the top of his staff
questions.evidence: I saw the steel butt of a pistol sticking from under the flap of his coat-pocket

questions.q: Why did the blind man keep edging up to David and asking if he was rich?
choices: He wanted to rob David
He wanted David to be his servant
He wanted to take David to church
He was trying to find his way by touch

questions.q: How did David finally get rid of the blind catechist?
choices: He ran away from him across a bog
He said he would shoot him with his own pistol
He paid him a dram of brandy to go away
He asked a passing drover to send him off
questions.evidence: I had a pistol in my pocket as well as he

questions.q: What did the innkeeper at Torosay tell David about the blind man, Duncan Mackiegh?
choices: That he was a harmless teacher loved by all the children
That he was a very dangerous man accused of robbery and murder
That he was really a spy working secretly for the Campbells of Mull
That he was not truly blind but only pretended to be
questions.evidence: That is a very dangerous man

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: David's journey across Mull, meeting both kind people and rogues
David searching every village on Mull for the lost crew
David working on a farm to earn money for a boat home
David and Alan hiding together from soldiers on Mull
questions.evidence: having travelled the greater part of that big and crooked Island of Mull, from Earraid to Torosay
